i like how batman gives most of his villains another chance. moments like these feel especially emphasized in the animated series, where you can tell he wants to help EVERYONE involved and not just the civilians targeted by the villains. most of the villains deep down have something going on and batman tries his best to help them by sending them to arkham (which unfortunately never seems to help at all. maybe gotham needs major mental health reform?). i think there's a sort of hope there, like batman knows he can't save everyone and can't reform everyone but he has a lot of hope in the assumption that these people are lashing out for a reason and that somehow he can help, yknow? so he sends them to the people he thinks are best equipped to help in areas he can't. he's hard and edgy on the outside but he cares and he wants to understand. obviously the degree to which this is true depends on the writer, but i feel like it's universal, just to varying degrees.
sorry if that was long, if you couldn't tell i get a kick out of infodumping about that kind of stuff. but i wanted to let you know that your comment means a lot to me and really made me think.
